finding_key: packages/documentation/guide/collaboration.md::collaboration doc scopes the comments side panel to documents only, but sheets also has one

verdict.reasoning: The new section in packages/documentation/guide/collaboration.md is headed "### The comments panel (documents)" and describes opening it only "In a document…", implying the panel is docs-only. The supplied sheets code contradicts that scoping: packages/sheets/src/view/shortcuts-catalog.ts (Comments category) lists `Mod+Alt+Shift+M` → "Toggle comments side panel" in a file whose header calls it the "single source of truth for the keyboard shortcuts shipped by the sheets editor", and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx has a keydown handler for Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+M that fires `onToggleCommentsPanel`, plus a `commentJumpTarget` prop for jumping from a thread list to a cell. The reviewer's detail that sheet-view.tsx renders `CommentSidePanel` is inaccurate — sheet-view.tsx only renders `CommentPopover` and delegates the toggle to a parent-supplied callback — and I could not see the parent that hosts the panel, so I cannot fully confirm the sheets panel UI ships. The core claim (a docs-coverage gap: sheets also has a comments side panel/shortcut the doc doesn't mention) is nonetheless supported by the code shown; impact is limited to documentation completeness.

finding_key: packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md::new docs page misstates the datasource access model: collaborators can execute queries with the owner's stored credentials

verdict.reasoning: The new page's "Good to know" bullet (datasources.md, last section) says the connection "belongs to the person who created it" and that collaborators "run their own connection to execute it", implying the creator's credentials are private to them. The supplied backend code contradicts that: `POST datasources/:id/query` in datasource.controller.ts only does `findRaw` + `workspaceService.assertMember(ds.workspaceId, userId)` (no author/role check — assertMember accepts any membership row regardless of role), and `DataSourceService.executeQuery` builds the client via `createClient(ds)` with `decrypt(ds.password)`, i.e. the creator's stored credentials. So any workspace member can run arbitrary validated SELECTs against the creator's PostgreSQL instance, which is the opposite of the documented model. I could not inspect the frontend datasource-view UI (not supplied), but the API-level behaviour is definitive for the doc's assertion; the defect is documentation-only, hence major rather than critical.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.controller.ts::any workspace member can steal another member's stored db password by re-pointing a datasource's host and hitting /test

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied sources (no checkout was mounted, so I read the file bodies provided). `DataSourceController.update` and `testConnection`/`executeQuery` (datasource.controller.ts, the `@Patch('datasources/:id')` and `@Post('datasources/:id/test')` handlers) gate only on `workspaceService.assertMember`, which in workspace.service.ts checks membership existence with no role or authorship constraint; `DataSourceService.update` freely accepts `host`/`port`/`database`/`username`/`sslEnabled` while leaving the stored encrypted `password` untouched, and `createClient` then does `password: decrypt(ds.password)` with `ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }`. So any workspace member can re-point another member's datasource at a host they control and trigger a connect, at which point node-pg will hand over the decrypted password (cleartext on `AuthenticationCleartextPassword`) — the exfiltration chain the claim describes is real and nothing in the module performs an ownership check. Caveat on scope rather than correctness: this backend code is untouched by the diff (the PR only adds `sheets/datasources.md`, whose "the connection belongs to the person who created it" line is what surfaced the issue), so the defect is pre-existing; I rate it major rather than critical because an attacker must already be a workspace member who can run the same queries through the app, but harvesting the raw credential escalates beyond the app's read-only SQL guard.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::datasource ssl uses rejectunauthorized:false, so the documented "ssl" toggle gives no mitm protection

verdict.reasoning: The quoted code is present verbatim in the supplied packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts (`createClient`: `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false`), so enabling the toggle yields encrypted-but-unauthenticated TLS; since `password: decrypt(ds.password)` is sent in the startup handshake, an active on-path attacker can harvest it and tamper with rows. The new doc page's "**SSL** — toggle on if your database requires it" bullet (datasources.md, Connect a database step 2) does not qualify this, so the documentation-misrepresentation angle also holds. Bounding the severity: the line is pre-existing and untouched by this docs-only diff, the toggle still stops passive sniffing, and exploitation needs a network position between the backend and a user-chosen DB host. I could not confirm the exact line number 204, only that the code sits at the end of `createClient`.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::"read-only" guarantee advertised by the new docs page rests on a bypassable sql keyword denylist

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied sources: sql-validator.ts:1-13 and 38-58 implement only a first-token SELECT/WITH check plus a fixed keyword denylist, and datasource.service.ts `executeQuery` wraps the raw `dto.query` in `SELECT * FROM (...) AS _q LIMIT`. Nothing blocks side-effecting or SSRF-capable function calls reachable from a SELECT (`pg_read_file`, `lo_import`, `dblink`, `pg_terminate_backend`, `setval`, `pg_sleep`), and COPY/DO/CALL/MERGE are indeed absent from the denylist — so the core technical claim is correct about the code as written. The claim's secondary "validator/executor text divergence" argument is overstated: the comment/string stripping makes the validator see *more* text (false positives), and I could not derive a bypass from it. Impact is bounded — every path goes through `assertMember`, and the credentials are ones a workspace member entered for their own DB, so this is member-vs-member privilege reach rather than an open hole, and the docs line at datasources.md:37 reads more like a UI statement ("can't edit, sort, or filter the cells in place") than a security guarantee; sql-validator.ts is also untouched by this PR.
